Review.Independence: The same agent that wrote reviews 1 to 5, which took no part in authoring or implementing the change or its fixes and saw nothing of those conversations. A deliberately small pass. It covers the complete diff a3d2b7d..2e90a3a (90 files): everything read for reviews 1 to 5, plus the two commits since. fc30c26 adds records only. 2e90a3a was read in full: seven files, one line each, replacing the two evidence column headings in the template and the five example pages and wording the evidence row of brief.md to match; no attribute, meta element, style rule or source file is touched. Given beyond the skill's hand-over: the author's description of that commit, checked against the diff, and the instruction not to rerun the full test suite without a reason. Rerun at 2e90a3a and exited 0: `bun run check`, `bun run examples:verify` and `bun run package:verify`. `bun test` was not rerun, because the diff changes only heading text: the conformance helper takes only the style block of the template, and the one test that loads example pages (FS-14, D-trace-boot and defective-brief) reads their attributes through check, which the headings cannot affect; for CK2 I rely on the receipt run-7 and its log (59 pass, 1 skipped, 0 fail), and where a Resolution below says a test passes in run-7 it means that log. The log hashes of all four checks match run-7. status reports revision 1, approved for execution, a clean candidate, no protected path and the one outside write. Review 5 as committed was not compared by hash. No probes or mutations: no kernel code changed. Limits: neither the approval of revision 1 nor the rejection of revision 2 was compared with its conversation; the recorded words of the rejection ("Let's keep it") are read by the record as declining the removal, which errs on the side of the approved text; the example pages still say they were written by an independent reader and I cannot tell who made the last edits; K1 rests on the targeted search of review 1; the interrupted-receipt path cannot be exercised on Windows; CK5 has no recorded observation; packages/** and cli-reference.md are covered by the byte comparison of CK4. K5 has no rule file and no Rule element; it is upheld, with the residue in F13.
